title: Act on the Training and Support of Regional Physicians
title_original: 지역의사의 양성 및 지원 등에 관한 법률
full_text:
ACT ON THE TRAINING AND SUPPORT OF REGIONAL PHYSICIANS

Article 1 (Purpose)
The purpose of this Act is to address regional imbalances in medical personnel and contribute to improving the quality of regional medical care by training physicians to work in medical institutions and other facilities in areas experiencing shortages of medical personnel and by prescribing basic matters necessary for their management.

Article 2 (Definitions)
The terms used in this Act are defined as follows:
1. The term "regional physician" means a person falling under either of the following:
(a) A person selected through the regional physician admission track under subparagraph 2, who has graduated from the relevant educational program and obtained a physician's license under Article 5 of the Medical Service Act, and who is obligated to work in a specified area for a certain period (hereinafter referred to as a "service-obligation regional physician");
(b) A physician qualified as a medical specialist under Article 77 of the Medical Service Act (hereinafter referred to as a "medical specialist") who has entered into a contract with the State or a local government and a medical institution to practice in a specified area for a certain period (hereinafter referred to as a "contract-based regional physician").
2. The term "regional physician admission track" means a university admission track operated by the head of a university to select persons seeking to become service-obligation regional physicians.
3. The term "mandatory service institution" means a medical institution at which a service-obligation regional physician actually works in the area where that physician is required to work for a certain period.

Article 3 (Relationship with Other Acts)
① Matters concerning regional physicians prescribed by this Act shall be governed by this Act in preference to other Acts.
② Except as otherwise provided by this Act concerning the regional physician admission track and students admitted through such a track, the Higher Education Act shall apply.

Article 4 (Regional Physician Admission Track)
① Where the head of a university located in an area prescribed by Presidential Decree and operating an educational program in medicine selects students for admission to that program under Article 34 of the Higher Education Act, the head shall select a specified proportion prescribed by Presidential Decree through the regional physician admission track.
② Of the persons admitted through the regional physician admission track, at least the proportion prescribed by Presidential Decree shall be selected from among persons satisfying all of the following requirements:
1. The person shall have graduated from a middle school and a high school located in the area where the relevant medical school is situated or an adjacent area prescribed by Presidential Decree (graduation means completion of the entire course of study from admission through graduation and includes persons expected to graduate in the case of high school);
2. The person shall have resided, during the period of attendance at the middle school and high school referred to in subparagraph 1, in the area where each such school is located.
③ The proportion for the regional physician admission track prescribed by Presidential Decree under paragraph ① shall be determined considering, among other things, the number of medical institutions and the shortage of medical personnel in each Special Metropolitan City, Metropolitan City, Special Self-Governing City, Do, or Special Self-Governing Province (hereinafter referred to as a "City/Do"), the distribution of medically underserved areas under Article 12 of the Public Health and Medical Services Act, the regional distribution of universities operating educational programs in medicine, and the supply-and-demand estimates of the Supply and Demand Estimation Committee under Article 23-2 of the Framework Act on Health and Medical Services.
④ Students admitted through the regional physician admission track may be required to complete additional programs prescribed by Presidential Decree, including courses in public medical services and field practice within the region.
⑤ Other matters necessary for the regional physician admission track shall be prescribed by Presidential Decree.

Article 5 (Support for Tuition and Related Expenses)
① The State and local governments shall provide students admitted through the regional physician admission track with support for admission fees, tuition, textbook expenses, dormitory fees, and other expenses prescribed by Presidential Decree (hereinafter referred to as "tuition and related expenses").
② Matters necessary for support for tuition and related expenses under paragraph ① shall be prescribed by Presidential Decree.

Article 6 (Suspension of Support for, and Return of, Tuition and Related Expenses)
① Where a person receiving support for tuition and related expenses under Article 5 falls under grounds prescribed by Presidential Decree, such as taking a leave of absence or repeating an academic year, such support shall be suspended for the period concerned.
② A person who has received support under Article 5 shall return the amount of tuition and related expenses received, together with interest calculated at the statutory interest rate under Article 379 of the Civil Act (hereinafter referred to as the "repayment amount"), if any of the following applies:
1. The person is removed from the student register, including by expulsion, or withdraws voluntarily;
2. The person fails to pass the national examination for physicians under Article 9 of the Medical Service Act within three years after graduation from the relevant educational program;
3. The person's physician's license is revoked during the mandatory service period under Article 7;
4. The person fails to perform the mandatory service in violation of Article 7.
③ Where a person has repaid the repayment amount on grounds under paragraph ② 2 and subsequently passes the national examination for physicians, the repayment amount paid shall be refunded to that person; provided, the provisions on mandatory service under Article 7 shall apply.
④ Notwithstanding paragraph ②, all or part of the repayment amount need not be returned where the grounds under any subparagraph of that paragraph arise from unavoidable circumstances prescribed by Presidential Decree, including illness, physical or mental disability, or death.
⑤ In the case of paragraph ② 3, the Minister of Health and Welfare may reduce or exempt the repayment amount in consideration of the period of mandatory service performed, as prescribed by Presidential Decree.
⑥ If a repayment amount is not returned under paragraph ②, it may be collected in the same manner as compulsory collection of national taxes.
⑦ Other matters necessary for suspension of support for tuition and related expenses, payment of repayment amounts, methods of calculation thereof, and related matters shall be prescribed by Presidential Decree.

Article 7 (Mandatory Service)
① A service-obligation regional physician shall serve for ten years in an area prescribed by Presidential Decree in consideration of the proportion of students admitted through the regional physician admission track under Article 4 for the location of the university from which the physician graduated and other factors (hereinafter referred to as the "mandatory service area") (such service is hereinafter referred to as "mandatory service"). In such case, notwithstanding Article 11 (1) of the Medical Service Act, the Minister of Health and Welfare may attach to the physician's license a condition requiring mandatory service in the mandatory service area for a period not exceeding ten years.
② When selecting students through the regional physician admission track under Article 4, the head of a university shall also announce the mandatory service area, among the mandatory service areas, in which service-obligation regional physicians graduating from that university will be required to perform mandatory service.
③ The Minister of Health and Welfare may determine and publicly notify the types and scope of medical institutions at which service-obligation regional physicians may perform mandatory service in mandatory service areas, after hearing the opinions of the Mayor of a Special Metropolitan City, the Mayor of a Metropolitan City, the Mayor of a Special Self-Governing City, the Governor of a Do, or the Governor of a Special Self-Governing Province (hereinafter referred to as the "Mayor/Do Governor") and relevant experts.
④ Where a service-obligation regional physician falls under any of the following, the relevant period shall be excluded from the mandatory service period:
1. The period during which the physician is enlisted or called up to fulfill military service obligations under the Military Service Act;
2. The period of training to obtain qualification as a medical specialist under Article 77 of the Medical Service Act; provided, the periods classified as follows shall be included in the mandatory service period:
(a) The entirety of the training period where the physician trains at a training hospital located in the physician's mandatory service area in a medical specialty determined and publicly notified by the Minister of Health and Welfare in consideration of regional health and medical needs and other factors;
(b) One-half of the training period where the physician trains at a training hospital located in the physician's mandatory service area in a specialty other than those under item (a);
3. The period during which the physician fails to comply with a corrective order issued under this Act;
4. The period during which the qualification or effect of the physician's license is suspended or the license is revoked under this Act or the Medical Service Act;
5. Any other period falling under grounds prescribed by Ordinance of the Ministry of Health and Welfare, including leave of absence.
⑤ Matters necessary for calculation of the mandatory service period, including its commencement date and methods of calculation, shall be prescribed by Ordinance of the Ministry of Health and Welfare.

Article 8 (Resident Training)
① The Minister of Health and Welfare may determine the types of medical specialties and the geographical scope of training hospitals that a service-obligation regional physician may select to obtain qualification as a medical specialist under Article 77 of the Medical Service Act, taking into account regional health and medical needs and the distribution of training hospitals by specialty.
② The types of medical specialties and the geographical scope of training hospitals under paragraph ① shall be prescribed by Ordinance of the Ministry of Health and Welfare.

Article 9 (Changes to Mandatory Service Areas)
Where a service-obligation regional physician wishes to change their mandatory service area for unavoidable reasons, the physician shall obtain approval from the Minister of Health and Welfare as prescribed by Ordinance of the Ministry of Health and Welfare. In such case, the Minister shall consult with the relevant Mayor/Do Governor.

Article 10 (Contract Procedures and Periods for Contract-Based Regional Physicians)
① The head of a local government may select medical institutions intending to conclude a contract under Article 2, subparagraph 1 (b).
② The head of a medical institution selected under paragraph ① shall publicly announce terms such as the medical specialties to be handled by the medical specialist and the contract period, as well as measures to be taken if such terms are not fulfilled. The contract period shall be a period prescribed by Presidential Decree within a range of not less than five years and not more than ten years.
③ The head of a local government may enter into a contract under Article 2, subparagraph 1 (b) with a medical specialist employed by a medical institution selected under paragraph ① pursuant to the announcement under paragraph ②.
④ Other matters necessary for employment and contracts of contract-based regional physicians shall be prescribed by Ordinance of the Ministry of Health and Welfare.

Article 11 (Prohibition of Concurrent Employment of Regional Physicians)
① Until completing mandatory service, a service-obligation regional physician may not work at a medical institution outside the physician's mandatory service area or at a medical institution other than one referred to in Article 7 (3); provided, this restriction shall not apply to work undertaken for resident training.
② Until the contract period expires, a contract-based regional physician may not work at a medical institution other than the medical institution with which a contract under Article 2, subparagraph 1 (b) was concluded (hereinafter referred to as the "contracting institution").

Article 12 (Support for Regional Physicians)
① The Minister of Health and Welfare and heads of local governments may provide regional physicians with support for housing, job-related education, career development, career choices, overseas training, and other matters to foster a sense of mission for regional health and medical services and encourage continued service.
② The Minister of Health and Welfare, heads of local governments, heads of mandatory service institutions, and heads of contracting institutions may grant preferential treatment, such as priority employment in the relevant institutions or in public health and medical institutions in the region (meaning public health and medical institutions under Article 2, subparagraph 3 of the Public Health and Medical Services Act), to regional physicians who have completed mandatory service or whose contract periods have expired.
③ Where a regional physician who has completed mandatory service or whose contract period has expired wishes to establish and operate a medical institution in a medically underserved area under Article 12 of the Public Health and Medical Services Act within the relevant City/Do, the Mayor/Do Governor may provide necessary administrative and financial support.

Article 13 (Suspension of Support for Regional Physicians)
Where a regional physician receiving support under Article 12 (1) becomes unable to work on any of the following grounds, such support may be suspended for the relevant period as prescribed by Presidential Decree; provided, support shall be suspended where subparagraph 2 applies:
1. The regional physician is enlisted or called up to fulfill military service obligations under the Military Service Act;
2. The qualification or effect of the regional physician's license is suspended under this Act or Article 66 of the Medical Service Act;
3. The regional physician receives training to obtain qualification as a medical specialist under Article 77 of the Medical Service Act (excluding the period of training under Article 7 (4) 2 (a));
4. Other grounds prescribed by Ordinance of the Ministry of Health and Welfare, including leave of absence.

Article 14 (Establishment and Operation of Regional Physician Support Centers)
① The Minister of Health and Welfare may establish and operate a Regional Physician Support Center (hereinafter referred to as the "Support Center") to perform duties relating to support for regional physicians under Article 12, including job-related education, career development, and career choices.
② The Minister of Health and Welfare may entrust the establishment and operation of the Support Center to an institution or organization prescribed by Presidential Decree. In such case, the Minister may support all or part of the expenses necessary for its operation.
③ Other matters necessary for the establishment and operation of the Support Center shall be prescribed by Ordinance of the Ministry of Health and Welfare.

Article 15 (Submission of Data)
① The Minister of Health and Welfare or a Mayor/Do Governor may request the head of a medical institution where a regional physician works to submit data on the physician's work status as prescribed by Ordinance of the Ministry of Health and Welfare, and the head of that institution shall not refuse such a request without good cause.
② Where necessary to verify the actual working status of regional physicians, the Minister of Health and Welfare may request relevant institutions to submit data on the physicians' work status, and the heads of those institutions shall not refuse such requests without good cause.
③ Where any of the following circumstances arises, a service-obligation regional physician shall report it to the competent Mayor/Do Governor and the Minister of Health and Welfare as prescribed by Ordinance of the Ministry of Health and Welfare:
1. The physician begins mandatory service;
2. Grounds under any subparagraph of Article 7 (4) arise or cease to exist;
3. The physician changes mandatory service institutions within the mandatory service area.

Article 16 (Corrective Orders)
Where the head of a mandatory service institution or a service-obligation regional physician falls under any of the following in connection with mandatory service, the Minister of Health and Welfare or a Mayor/Do Governor may, as prescribed by Ordinance of the Ministry of Health and Welfare, order correction within a specified period:
1. A service-obligation regional physician violates Article 7 (1), Article 9, Article 11 (1), or Article 15 (3);
2. The head of a medical institution refuses to submit data in violation of Article 15 (1).

Article 17 (Suspension and Revocation of Licenses)
① Where a service-obligation regional physician fails to comply with a corrective order under Article 16, the Minister of Health and Welfare may suspend the physician's license qualification for a period not exceeding one year as prescribed by Ordinance of the Ministry of Health and Welfare.
② Where a service-obligation regional physician has been subject to suspension of license qualification under paragraph ① at least three times or fails to perform mandatory service in violation of Article 7, the Minister of Health and Welfare may revoke the physician's license as prescribed by Ordinance of the Ministry of Health and Welfare.
③ Before revoking a physician's license under paragraph ②, the Minister of Health and Welfare shall hold a hearing.
④ A person whose physician's license has been revoked under paragraph ② may not have the license reissued, during the remaining period of mandatory service calculated from the revocation date, except on condition that the person will perform mandatory service.

Article 18 (Administrative Fines)
① Any person who fails to comply with a corrective order under Article 16 shall be subject to an administrative fine not exceeding ten million won.
② Any of the following persons shall be subject to an administrative fine not exceeding five million won:
1. The head of a medical institution who fails to submit or falsely submits data on the working status of a regional physician without good cause in violation of Article 15 (1);
2. A service-obligation regional physician who fails to report or falsely reports circumstances concerning work in violation of Article 15 (3).
③ Administrative fines under paragraphs ① and ② shall be imposed and collected by the Minister of Health and Welfare or a Mayor/Do Governor as prescribed by Presidential Decree.

Article 19 (Delegation of Authority and Entrustment of Affairs)
① Part of the authority of the Minister of Health and Welfare or a Mayor/Do Governor under this Act may be delegated to a Mayor/Do Governor or the head of a Si, Gun, or Gu as prescribed by Presidential Decree.
② Part of the affairs of the Minister of Health and Welfare or a Mayor/Do Governor under this Act may be entrusted to the head of a mandatory service institution or a contracting institution as prescribed by Presidential Decree.

ADDENDA <Act No. 21239, Dec. 23, 2025>

This Act shall enter into force on the date two months after its promulgation.
